bullets.text: The wind-driven Redpine Fire ignited in the Redpine National Forest near Hollis Ridge on August 18, 2025, and grew from 40 hectares to over 9,500 hectares in five days.
The fire jumped Route 9 and burned into the town of Ashford Mill, destroying 48 structures including 31 homes and forcing a mandatory evacuation of the town and surrounding zones.
No lives were lost; injuries were limited to two firefighters treated for heat exhaustion, smoke-related respiratory cases, and one returning resident burned by smoldering debris.
Wildfire reported in the Redpine National Forest near Hollis Ridge, estimated at 40 hectares and growing fast in gusty winds.
The fire jumps Route 9 toward Ashford Mill; mandatory evacuation ordered for the town and zones C1-C4.
Route 9 was closed through the fire area, later reopening with pilot cars.
A mandatory evacuation was ordered for all of Ashford Mill and zones C1-C4, with residents told to leave immediately via Route 9 south.
The fire exhibited extreme behavior early on, crowning through pines on Hollis Ridge under 60 km/h gusts and jumping Route 9.
Growth progressed from 40 to 1,800 to 4,600 to 9,200 hectares over the first three days before slowing.
The sheriff's office issued a mandatory evacuation order for Ashford Mill and zones C1-C4, followed by get-set warnings for Larkin Springs.
Fear dominated the evacuation phase, with residents describing ember-strewn escape drives, giving way to cautious optimism as containment grew.
